description:
`Distill.main(System.argv())` after a defmodule -> parse error at item position (frontdoor.rs:152; parse_item accepts only items and Ident-headed macro calls). Every path submits root main/0 (cli.rs:663, :699).

Decision (2026-10-17): a file's top-level expressions become the program's main/0, in order, after all definitions are published (a superset of Elixir). A file with both top-level expressions and its own main/0 is a compile error naming both. Files with only def main() are unchanged.

Design (page /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.5.html; APPROVED 2026-10-18). The parser cannot tell a statement from a macro item (def/test/user macros are plain identifiers; `test` is a macro only under fz2 test); expansion already decides "not a macro" and today turns it into item_macro_not_defmacro. So:
1. Parser: at file top level only (empty module path, Eof terminator) parse_item accepts any expression start; defmodule bodies keep the refusal.
2. Surface: a top-level item that is not a call node becomes ScopeForm::Statement; call-shaped items stay MacroCall (incl. remote calls).
3. Expansion: in a submitted file's top-level scope (current_module.is_global() && !world.is_prelude(owner)), a form that is not a macro is recorded in the ScopeSession as a statement, in walk order; elsewhere item_macro_not_defmacro fires as today.
4. End of ScopeSession::publish (that scope only), when statements exist: if main/0 is also reserved -> new diagnostic resolve/script-and-main (primary: first statement; secondary: the def main), code in src/diag/codes.rs + codes_test.rs; else synthesize def main() with the statements as one __block__ (single statement bare), span first..last, published via define_source_function.
Tests: frontdoor_test (top level accepts expressions, defmodule still refuses, test(:name) do..end stays one item); oracle fixture (script run by elixir) with kind: run covering defmodule then statements, binding flow, remote call, forward call to a later def, literal statement; diagnostic fixture for script + def main; fz2 test discovery unchanged.
Predicted: no existing fixture, pin or golden moves; no new job.
Removal: top-level "does not yet parse … at item position" refusal; item_macro_not_defmacro in a submitted file's top-level scope.
Docs: pipeline.md, parser-syntax.md, fixtures.md, guides/modules.html, README if it describes program shape.
Decision (2026-10-23): a top-level macro call whose expansion is not a definition form is a statement too, in walk order, wherever the macro comes from ( runs as in Elixir; a same-file macro used at the top level, an Elixir compile error, also works: one rule, a superset of Elixir). Fixture covers a remote expression macro at the top level.
title: Script mode: a file's top-level expressions run in order
